text:
A patient may need a tracheostomy, a surgical opening in the neck into the windpipe, when they need a reliable airway or long-term breathing support. Common reasons include prolonged mechanical ventilation that can't be weaned, upper airway obstruction from tumours, trauma, or severe swelling, and an inability to protect the airway or clear secretions after stroke, severe head injury, or neuromuscular disease.

CONFIDENCE: 90
